text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Pope John Paul II managed to carry out his agenda despite inclement weather during his two-day visit to Hungary on the weekend.
- President Arpad Goncz appointed Tamas Suchman Minister of Industry and Trade effective September 5.
- Parliament will resume sitting on Tuesday and the House will hold an unscheduled session on Wednesday to hear an address by King Juan Carlos of Spain.

- At the Hungarian-German economic forum on Friday, Prime Minister Gyula Horn pledged further benefits to foreign investors and promised to honour the pledges made to energy industry investors by introducing cost-effective prices early next year.
- Addressing an economic forum hosted by the Free Democrats, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy warned yesterday that there is a growing danger that the government's economic policy is softening.
- The Finance Ministry has issued a statement denying claims made by the Smallholders Party that the government is planning a one-time, large-scale devaluation of the forint in the near future.
- Prime Minister and Socialist Party President Gyula Horn arrived in New York Sunday to take part in the 20th Congress of the Socialist International.
- The Hungarian defence minister and his Romanian counterpart on Friday signed a confidence building and security agreement in Arad, Romania.
- After a slight dip in July, the manufacturing sector experienced an upswing in August, as the Procurement Manager Index rose above the critical 50 per cent threshold to 52.7 per cent in August.
- Insurance companies in Hungary attained a collective HUF 75 billion in first-half gross revenues from fees from 12.2 million policies. (Sat.)
- Shareholders of the wine company Egervin have approved a private capital increase of nearly 50 per cent to HUF 500 million.
- As of today, all trading on the Budapest Stock Exchange will occur by way of computerised automatic transaction, completely replacing the former open outcry system.
- Pop star Michael Jackson arrived yesterday to give concert at the Nepstadion Tuesday evening.
NEPSZABADSAG

- MPs for the Democratic Federation of Hungarians in Romania are unanimously dissatisfied with the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty as it does not meet the requirements of the Hungarian community in Romania.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Hungarian agriculture minister has signed a long-term bilateral trade cooperation agreement with his Algerian counterpart.
- The Ferenc Liszt International Piano Contest will open in Budapest today.
NEPSZAVA
- A new poll gives the Young Democrats their highest support in years, placing them a close third with 21 per cent, behind the Socialists with 24 per cent and the Smallholders with 23 per cent.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- American Life Insurance Co., part of America's AIG group, has boosted its 88 per cent stake in the First American-Hungarian Insurance Rt to full ownership. (Sat.)
